summary: SEMI's Q1 2026 billings of $36.6B (+14% YoY) and its July mid-year forecast of $165.9B in 2026 equipment sales (+23% YoY) remain the latest official industry data this month, with DRAM/HBM buildouts still the primary growth driver and no downward revision in evidence. The capital cycle continues to run at record pace, supporting sustained test-tool order flow through year-end.

The four largest hyperscalers now guide to roughly $725-750B of 2026 capex, with Microsoft citing an $80B unfulfilled Azure backlog on power constraints and both Alphabet and Meta raising their ceilings again this earnings season. Compute buildouts remain supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained, keeping AI-accelerator test capacity the strongest pillar of order confidence even as hyperscaler free cash flow compresses.
sources: [Futurum: AI Capex 2026](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/ai-capex-2026-the-690b-infrastructure-sprint/) ; [Seeking Alpha: hyperscaler capex Aug 2026](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4929289-4-hyperscalers-one-message-the-ai-trade-isnt-over)

summary: Microchip Technology guided Q2 revenue and EPS above Street estimates on strengthening automotive and industrial demand, with management now describing automotive as beginning a genuine recovery rather than merely working through destocking. Tightening lead times and early signs of possible device undersupply suggest restocking could start reversing the push-out pattern that has weighed on ATE bookings for two years, though the recovery is still nascent.
sources: [Yahoo Finance: Microchip forecasts upbeat revenue](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/microchip-tech-forecasts-upbeat-quarterly-215115053.html) ; [Nemo: automotive semiconductor recovery](https://explore.nemo.money/en/insights/microchip-technology-revenue-outlook-automotive-chip-demand-2026)

summary: S&P Global's US Manufacturing PMI eased to 53.2 in August on higher fuel costs and reduced inventory building, and ISM's index stayed contractionary at 48.7, so the headline macro trend remains soft. Bottoms-up signals are more encouraging, though: Cohu reported industrial-segment orders up 87% YoY in Q2, suggesting the destocking-driven order drought in industrial test may be starting to lift.
sources: [S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI, August 2026](https://www.pmi.spglobal.com/Public/Home/PressRelease/c1430bf93dfa42d3bb8927edf49494db) ; [Motley Fool: Cohu Q2 2026 earnings call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/03/cohu-cohu-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)

summary: IDC has revised its 2026 smartphone shipment forecast down further to a record 16.7% decline (from 13.9% last quarter), with second-half shipments now expected to fall 27.2% YoY as NAND/DRAM costs up over 300% YoY hit the sub-$100 segment hardest. The memory-driven demand destruction is worsening rather than stabilizing, deepening the drag on mobile test volume and the risk of further capacity redeployment.
sources: [IDC: smartphone shipments to drop 16.7% in 2026](https://www.idc.com/resource-center/blog/smartphone-shipments-set-for-record-16-7-drop-in-2026-as-the-memory-crisis-hits-full-force/) ; [Asymco: what's going on with smartphones](https://asymco.com/2026/08/20/whats-going-on-with-smartphones/)

summary: Chinese OSATs posted first-half profit growth of up to 317% and ASE has raised advanced-packaging quotes over 20% as AI/HBM packaging soaks up capacity, but that same tightness is squeezing the packaging slots available to automotive, industrial, and consumer customers. Excess inventory itself is largely clean industry-wide, so the constraint is shifting from excess stock to capacity allocation - a mixed signal for ATE utilization outside AI-linked accounts.
sources: [Digitimes: Chinese OSAT earnings surge](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260831VL201/profit-packaging-earnings-demand-revenue.html) ; [Silicon Analysts: semiconductor repricing wave](https://siliconanalysts.com/analysis/semiconductor-repricing-wave-price-hikes-reshape-chip-supply-chain)

summary: Advantest raised FY26 guidance on an expected 44% tester-market expansion despite a quarter-on-quarter SoC dip from pulled-forward Q1 deliveries, while Teradyne guided Q3 revenue to $1.2-1.3B on top of a record AI-driven Q2. Cohu's $850M HPC pipeline and 87% YoY growth in industrial orders show the test-demand upcycle broadening beyond AI-pure-play accounts, reinforcing confidence in Apex's addressable market growth.

The US-China truce reached after the late-2025 escalation has left China's rare-earth export controls suspended through November 10, 2026, and BIS continues case-by-case rather than presumptive-denial licensing for H200-class chips, easing near-term supply-chain disruption risk. Congressional efforts such as the AI OVERWATCH Act to add oversight of chip export licenses, plus the looming November truce expiration, keep this a live watch item rather than a resolved one.
sources: [Morgan Lewis: BIS export review policy](https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/01/bis-revises-export-review-policy-for-advanced-ai-chips-destined-for-china-and-macau) ; [CSIS: rare earth export restrictions one year later](https://www.csis.org/analysis/rare-earth-export-restrictions-one-year-later)

summary: On August 6 the administration added a new Section 232 action imposing tariffs and minimum import prices on polysilicon and its derivatives (effective December 2026), layered on top of the January 25% semiconductor tariff and its 2027 escalation deadline. Each new action adds landed-cost and purchase-price-variance uncertainty for customers sourcing test and fab inputs globally, signaling continued willingness to use Section 232 across the semiconductor supply chain.
sources: [White & Case: polysilicon Section 232 tariffs](https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/president-trump-orders-tariffs-and-price-floors-polysilicon-section-232-action) ; [Wiley: polysilicon Section 232 tariffs and MIPs](https://www.wiley.law/alert-Trump-Administration-Imposes-Section-232-Tariffs-and-Minimum-Import-Prices-on-Polysilicon-and-its-Derivatives)

summary: The US flash composite PMI jumped to 56 in August, its strongest reading since April 2022, as services strength offset a manufacturing slowdown, while China's high-tech manufacturing sub-index held at 52.9 in expansion even as its broader factory index stayed below 50. The macro backdrop is neutral-to-supportive: aggregate growth is resilient and tech-specific activity is outperforming general manufacturing, removing a modest headwind from last month's assessment.
sources: [InvestingLive: flash PMI August 2026](https://investinglive.com/news/s-p-global-manufacturing-pmi-flash-estimate-for-august-53-2-versus-53-9-estimate/) ; [Tech Times: China manufacturing PMI, AI hardware sub-index](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/326101/20260831/china-manufacturing-pmi-contracts-again-ai-hardware-sub-index-defies-slump.htm)
